AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: This study set out to identify significant lesion features of chronic total occlusion (CTO) that predict successful retrograde recanalization via epicardial collateral channels (CCs).

AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Epicardial CCs remain essential in retrograde percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of CTO. However, the unpredictability of success and occurrence of complications limit the application of epicardial CCs for retrograde PCI technique for CTO.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: 103 retro-recanalization cases were analyzed using epicardial CCs with successful recanalization as an end point. Clinical and angiography data were collected.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The total success rate was 76.3%. Independent predictors associated with technical success included CCs tortuosity, side branch at CCs tortuosity, inadequate CCs Size and inadequate CCs exit location. Assigning a score of one for each variable, four levels of difficulty were obtained and formed the EPI-CTO score (Epicardial CTO). This score had significant predictive value for the likelihood of successful recanalization (AUC: 0.94, 95%CI: 0.89-0.98). Coronary and CCs perforation occurred in 6 and 10 cases respectively. Four cases including two coronary and two CCs perforations had tamponade that needed pericardiocentesis.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Using epicardial CCs for retrograde approach of CTO PCI is effective. Complication rate was acceptable. We found four independent predictors relative to procedure success.
